To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) using a logarithmic quantization method to reduce the number of bits per feature vector can significantly decrease calibration and training time for machine learning algorithms without significantly decreasing classification accuracy; (2) using a progressive calibration method to reduce the amount of data used for machine learning algorithms can significantly decrease calibration time for machine learning classifiers without significantly decreasing classification performance; (3) using a progressive method of training a machine learning algorithm on a dataset of physiological signals can significantly decrease training time for machine classifiers; and
(1) the logarithmic quantization of the EEG signal can be used to reduce the feature vector size and (2) the progressive calibration technique can be used to decrease the calibration time.
